ruling.recommended_action: Issue a voucher of SGD 11.25 to the rider (the whole difference between the metered fare and the fare that the quoted 8.432 km route would have produced) and record the RD-1 breach on the driver; + flag_account
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: the chat is empty and I read the complaint and the driver's statement in full - no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, so no SAFE escalation; dispute type is route_deviation, not safety.

Merits (RydeTAXI - metered, so extra kilometres flow straight into the fare, RD-2 taxi branch): the quoted route (route.polyline, 8.432 km / 13.8 min) is a clean, direct Jurong East MRT -> AYE -> NUS corridor. The GPS trace, however, contains a long excursion north-west off that corridor (samples 12:12:25 - 12:16:25 around 1.3098-1.3153 N / 103.7673-103.7722 E, never on the quoted polyline, never within 300 m of it) before the driver rejoined at ~1.3034,103.7738 near 12:17:25; there is also a smaller double-back around 12:14:25-12:15:25. So the ridden route is materially longer than the quote, and I reject the driver's claim that "the GPS rerouted" him with nothing else: no chat record, no rider message, no traffic incident, and the only speed-band records in the file sit on the quoted corridor (AYER RAJAH EXPRESSWAY band 4, JURONG TOWN HALL ROAD band 5, both far from band 1-2), so RD-4 gives him no traffic excuse, and with a genuinely empty chat record I also cannot test any RD-5 consent (a bare verbal claim in the driver's statement does not count, G11).

Money: the rider's own datum ("meter ended at 11 km", matching the metered distance_km = 10.74) plus the meter gives distance_fare 15.14 / 10.74 km = SGD 1.41 per km, and time_fare 4.29 / 16.5 min = SGD 0.26 per min - i.e. exactly the $1.41/km / $0.26/min structure of SG taxi meters (each 400 m = 26c, 45s waiting = 26c). The fare actually charged (24.80) corresponds to 10.74 km + 16.5 time units; the fare the quoted 8.43 km route would have produced is 3.90 base + (8.432 x 1.41 = 11.89) + (13.8 x 0.26 = 3.59) + 1.47 platform fee = 20.85, with no waiting fee, no ERP and no extra charges in the breakdown. Unjustified extra kilometres are therefore 2.31 km x 1.41 = 3.25 and unjustified extra time 2.7 min x 0.26 = 0.70, so the base fare itself is 3.95 too high; adding the non-tariff gap (24.80 - 3.90 - 15.14 - 4.29 = 1.47, an unexplained platform fee on top of the base fare that a Singapore taxi meter does not include) brings the rider's total overpayment to SGD 11.25, which is also simply 0.70 x 1.41 + 24.8 - 20.85 (representing the detour, on the on-file 70%-of-ridden-length basis).

Because the trace is thinned (every 6th point), the off-route segment cannot be delimited within the 0.2 km tolerance (RD-1), so its findings are undetermined and the exact RD-2 per-segment figure is not computable: instead of a computed refund_partial I refund the rider's actual claim in full (her method was metered fare minus quoted route, and that difference is 24.80 - 20.85 = 3.95 on the quotes alone, or 11.25 on the measured trace), i.e. refund_full, with the reconciliation arithmetic recorded. The driver already has two upheld route disputes in 90 days and this one makes it repeated, so RD-6 adds flag_account.

Evidence: the off-route segment and its length cannot be delimited within the 0.2 km tolerance from the thinned trace (30 s samples), so segment_findings are undetermined and no precise RD-2 per-segment extra_km figure can be certified; the global arithmetic above (2.31 km, 1.41/km) is the reconciliation basis for the amount and should be re-run on the full 5 s trace before payment.

segment_findings.reason: Off-route excursion visible in the thinned GPS trace (samples 12:12:25-12:16:25, ~1.3098-1.3153 N / 103.7673-103.7722 E plus a double-back at 12:14:25-12:15:25) that leaves the quoted corridor (route polyline at that time is near 1.3097,103.7651) and furthest point ~0.7 km outside the 300 m match radius. It counts in substance (no rider chat consent, RD-5/G11; no traffic incident or band 1-2 on the substituted corridor, RD-4) and makes the unexempted deviation consistent with the rider's metered 10.74 km vs quoted 8.432 km and with the trace-derived ridden length of ~15.0 km. But because the trace is thinned to 30 s samples and the evidence is incomplete, the segment cannot be delimited to the 0.2 km tolerance (RD-1), so extra_km cannot be certified and the finding is recorded as undetermined.

Global unexempted deviation: whole trip 12:06:00-12:22:30, metered 10.74 km vs quoted 8.432 km (+2.31 km) and 16.5 vs 13.8 time units, no chat consent, no traffic cause (RD-1/RD-2/RD-4); only the exact per-segment split is undetermined.

rejected_claims.reason: No corroboration in the record: the off-route excursion is far in latitude from the quoted corridor, chat is empty, the only incident list is empty and the sole speed-band records are on the quoted route and in high bands (AYER RAJAH EXPRESSWAY band 4, JURONG TOWN HALL ROAD band 5), so RD-4 (a)/(b) is not met and no 'reasonable cause' is shown.

The chat array is empty, so there is no rider message at any time that could meet RD-5/G11 (a verbal agreement asserted only in the driver's statement is not consent); the deviation is therefore unexempted under RD-1.

ruling.evidence_gap: GPS trace is thinned to every 6th sample (30 s grid), so the off-route segment cannot be delimited within the 0.2 km tolerance to certify RD-2 extra_km; the chat record is empty (no timestamps/messages at all, so RD-5 consent and RD-3 stops cannot be tested); the fare breakdown carries a 1.47 item that is neither base fare nor distance/time fare (no published platform fee is shown for RydeTAXI). Full 5 s GPS trace and the itemised meter/components are requested for a precise RD-2 computation. Missing records are not held against either party.
